answer: Three cumulative conditions: (a) the relevant regulator or Relevant Resolution Authority (after consulting each other) has determined that Belfius Bank is failing or likely to fail; (b) having regard to timing and other circumstances, there is no reasonable prospect that alternative private sector measures or supervisory action would prevent the failure within a reasonable timeframe; (c) a resolution action is necessary in the public interest. The 'failing or likely to fail' determination can rest on four alternative circumstances (one or more present): (i) infringement (or objective elements of near-future infringement) of authorisation requirements justifying withdrawal of authorisation, incl. losses depleting all or a significant amount of own funds; (ii) assets are/will in the near future be less than liabilities; (iii) unable/likely unable to pay debts or liabilities as they fall due; (iv) requests extraordinary public financial support.

answer: Risk: hedging at Class level may expose the Fund to cross-contamination risk, as a counterparty's recourse may not be limited to the assets of the relevant Class; although costs, gains and losses accrue solely to the relevant Class, hedging transactions in one Class may negatively impact the NAV of another Class (particularly where EMIR/DF Act require the Fund to post initial/variation margin, posted at the Fund's risk, not the Class's), exposing investors in other Classes to a proportion of this risk (no segregation of liability between Classes). Limits: over-hedged positions must not exceed 105% of the NAV of the relevant Class; under-hedged positions must not fall short of 95% of the portion of the Class NAV that is to be hedged against currency risk.

evidence.text: Hedging activity at Class level may expose the Fund to cross contamination risk
Over-hedged positions should not exceed 105% of the Net Asset Value of the relevant Class;
Under-hedged positions should not fall short of 95% of the portion of the Net Asset Value of the relevant Class which is to be hedged against currency risk;

notes: The 95% floor applies to the portion of Class NAV to be hedged, not total NAV.
